passages.title: A difficult semester
passages.text: Last semester was hard for Sofía. She was studying engineering at a public university, and she was also working at a café three evenings a week. One night in November, while she was taking notes in the library, her phone rang. It was her manager. He said that he needed her at work immediately. Sofía told him that she had an important exam the next day, and he finally agreed to let her stay. Unfortunately, she failed that exam anyway, because she was too tired to concentrate. A few days later, her math professor asked her if everything was OK. Sofía explained her situation, and the professor told her about a scholarship for students who work. She applied, and two months later she got it. Now she doesn't have to work in the evenings. She hands in her homework on time, and she passed all her subjects in the spring. "I was trying to do everything alone," she says. "Asking for help was the best decision I made."

points: Pasado continuo («was / were» + -ing): una acción en curso en el pasado: «I was studying».
Con «when» + pasado simple, marcas lo que la interrumpió: «…when it began to rain».
«said» va sin la persona; «told» la lleva: «He told me to stand up».
«pass an exam» es aprobar; «take an exam» es presentarlo.

examples.en: What were you doing when it began to rain?
examples.es: ¿Qué estabas haciendo cuando empezó a llover?

mistake.note: «approve» es aprobar una idea o un plan; aprobar un examen es «pass».

points: En estilo indirecto el verbo suele retroceder un tiempo: «I'm tired» → «She said that she was tired».
Preguntas de sí o no: «asked if» o «asked whether» + sujeto + verbo, sin «do».
«hand in» es entregar una tarea; con pronombre: «hand it in».
«homework» es incontable: «a lot of homework», nunca con -s.
